text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Individual bank deposits of up to 10 million lei have been guaranteed starting September 2, said central bank's comunications department.
- Domestic electricity and heat consumption dropped by 30 percent over the last six years, according to a study made by Univers trade unions, including energy sector workers.
ADEVARUL
- Representatives of some 100 Romanian and foreign companies at investors' forum held in Bucharest this week complained about bureaucracy, chaotic legislation and taxation.
- Agriculture Minister Alexandru Lapusan will join the board of the Bank for Agriculture BARO, ruling Party of Social Democracy (PDSR) executive president Adrian Nastase said.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- World Bank confirmed support for Romanian health reforms after new minister was appointed two weeks ago.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Dissident Doina Cornea and her son has lodged a challenge with the Central Electoral Bureau against President Ion Iliescu's candidacy for a new presidential term.
- Iliescu's right to run for a new term has also been contested by the Civic Aliance group, who submitted a protest to the Central Electoral Bureau.
- U.S. First Lady Hillary Clinton sent a letter to Bucharest mayor Victor Ciorbea, thanking him for his hospitality during her visit to Romania in July.
ADEVARUL
- Former Prime Minister Petre Roman launched his presidential campaign for his Social Democratic Union (USD) party for the November elections.
- National Unity Party (PUNR) plans to introduce a motion in parliament to protest against the signing of the friendship treaty with Hungary.
- Doctors say meningitis epidemics has been contained.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- The newspaper says that Romania and Hungary signed "a historic" military treaty which will guarantee mutual control of troops deployed in the common border area.
- Opposition Democratic Convention bloc has less air time on public radio and state television, than Iliescu and Roman.
- The number of drugs dealers and addicts is sharply rising in Romania.
- President Iliescu, while on his re-election campaign trail in the norththeast town of Rimnicu Sarat, gave 20,000 lei to a local beggar.
ZIUA

- Dissident Doru Braia tied himself to a big stone cross in Bucharest's central University Square to protest against President Iliescu's seeking re-election in the November polls. The constitution of 1991 limits presidents to serving two four-year terms.
DIMINEATA
- The post-communist treaty between Romania and Hungary, which will be signed on September 16, rules out autonomy for ethnic minorities along ethnic lines and guarantees existing borders.
CRONICA ROMANA
- Finance ministry denies rumours of a looming rise of vegetable oil, tobacco and medical drugs prices.
JURNALUL NATIONAL
- Romania will not pay extradition fees for top model Catalin Botezatu, who has been detained by Italian police.
- Ruling PDSR party is looking for jobs for its MPs which will not run again in November's parliamentary polls. ($=3,177 lei)
